sources.title: Arabic CV: birth, 1992 agriculture degree, provincial and ministerial service
sources.findings: Read four-page Arabic CV hosted by Iraqi Institute for Economic Reform: Baghdad 1970, University of Baghdad agriculture bachelor 1992, agriculture service from June 4, 1997, Amarah local administration 2004, provincial council 2005–2009, governor 2009, human rights ministry December 2010, labour ministry September 8, 2014–October 24, 2018 and acting portfolios. Use month precision for December 2010 and year precision for 2009, not false precision from contradictory secondary term tables. Current-office text in this old CV is historical, not a 2026 mandate certification.

sources.title: Biographical chronology, updated December 2024; historical details cross-checked
sources.findings: Read Al Jazeera Arabic biography updated December 2024: Baghdad birth, family from Maysan, 1992 agriculture degree, local/provincial career, 2009 governorship, 2010–2014 human rights and 2014–2018 labour/social affairs. Distinguish acting portfolios. Its lead calls October 13, 2022 the start of premiership; contemporaneous UN and Turkish government accounts instead anchor confidence and government start on October 27. Not used as a current-role source. Founder/date accounts for Euphrates movement vary, so no precise founding date is adopted.

sources.title: Secretary-General welcomes government formed 27 October 2022
sources.findings: Read UN Iraq statement: October 27, 2022 government formation, 21 ministries filled including three women and two still vacant. Statement signed October 28 and local page dated October 29; neither publication date replaces the confidence date. Calls for reform/accountability are aspirations, not proof of achieved governance outcomes.

sources.publisher: Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.title: Contemporary confirmation of confidence vote, 27 October 2022
sources.findings: Read contemporaneous Turkish Foreign Ministry statement dated October 27, 2022 explicitly welcoming that day’s parliamentary confidence vote and Sudani assuming the premiership. Distinguish presidential designation earlier in October from approved government formation, and external diplomatic support from certification of domestic performance.

sources.title: Development Road announcement and proposed scale, 27 May 2023
sources.findings: Read VOA May 27, 2023 full transport-project announcement: Baghdad meeting, Gulf-to-Türkiye railway/road concept, proposed $17 billion and 1200 km, further discussions required. This is a plan/estimated scale, not a completed corridor or verified diversification result. Article does not establish that later financing, procurement or all construction phases were completed.

sources.title: 11 November 2025 election date and 46-seat coalition entry; other fields not adopted
sources.findings: Read IPU Parline 2025 election date, 329 total seats and coalition table entry 46. Page marks results unofficial and has inconsistent fields: 30.1% largest-party figure does not equal 46/329, turnout denominator also conflicts with electoral reporting. No turnout, percentage, other-party totals or complete-table accuracy claim adopted. Coalition seat count independently verified against Reuters quoting election commission.

sources.title: Election commission announces 46 seats for Sudani coalition, 17 November 2025
sources.findings: Read Reuters November 17, 2025 substantive final-results report: Sudani list 46 of 329, largest individual list but coalition-building still needed. General vote November 11, initial-result photos November 12 and commission announcement November 17 are distinct. A plurality does not confer direct popular election as prime minister or guarantee another term. No full certification/complaints record audit claimed.

sources.title: Coalition spokesperson confirms withdrawal from premiership contest, 12 January 2026
sources.findings: Read Rudaw January 12, 2026 named coalition-spokesperson account: leadership decided to withdraw Sudani’s candidacy in favour of Maliki to break Coordination Framework deadlock. This announcement did not end caretaker duties that day and did not make Maliki prime minister. Subsequent completed succession is separately documented.

sources.title: Zaidi sworn in with partial cabinet, 14 May 2026
sources.findings: Read Reuters May 14, 2026 article updated May 15: Ali al-Zaidi sworn in on Thursday, parliament approved 14 ministers with remaining portfolios unsettled. Parliamentary approval and oath differ from May 16 handover. No claim that the entire cabinet was complete or that a delayed portfolio vote prolonged Sudani’s full premiership.

sources.title: Formal handover and assumption of duties, 16 May 2026
sources.findings: Read Anadolu May 16, 2026 completed handover report citing INA, with April 27 designation and May 14 confidence context. Handover in Baghdad on May 16 establishes successor taking over duties from Sudani; do not call May 16 the earlier parliamentary oath date or adopt an unqualified single date for all stages.

sources.title: Masrour Barzani receives coalition leader and former federal premier, 12 October 2026
sources.findings: Read KRG official Arabic October 12, 2026 meeting report: Masrour Barzani receives former federal prime minister and Reconstruction and Development Coalition leader. Distinguish Masrour from Masoud Barzani. KRG budget demands and cooperation positions are not enacted federal budget allocations; no outcome figures adopted.

sources.title: Zaidi meets coalition leader Sudani, 2 November 2026
sources.findings: Read NINA November 2, 2026 substantive report quoting Zaidi’s media office: actual evening meeting with Sudani as coalition leader, discussing development, reform and anti-corruption. Current navigation on November 18 is not the meeting date. Claims of intended reform are not independent proof that corruption was eliminated.

sources.title: Sudani meets Bafel Talabani and Shaswar Abdulwahid, 12 November 2026
sources.findings: Read 964 Media November 12, 2026 completed meeting report and attributed Sudani-office statement: Bafel Talabani and Shaswar Abdulwahid visit him in Baghdad, with Haider al-Fawadi present. It supports recent personal political activity and coalition leadership, not renewed premiership, a finalized coalition agreement or enacted reforms.
